1.why: All eight screens are static card layouts with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups of any kind.

2.why: Bold headings, teal primary buttons, and the yellow phishing banner stand out clearly, though the critical recovery token is buried in small monospace text inside the Logs panel.

3.why: Each screen presents a single labeled task and button, but the required recovery token must be located inside the technical Logs panel, which hinders quick finding.

4.why: Step 4 imposes five password rules (12+ characters, uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol, no reuse) within a six-step flow, so many rules and steps must be remembered.

5.why: No password manager prompt, autofill hint, or 'remember me' option appears on any of the eight screens.

6.why: No saved, prefilled, or previously used items are surfaced anywhere; every input field is empty each time.

7.why: Instructions are one or two short sentences per screen, though phrases like 'account contact value' and 'simulated local delivery channel' introduce some jargon.

8.why: No error messages appear in any step of the flow, so there is no observable evidence that they describe problems and fixes.

9.why: The MFA code (482913) is displayed on-screen showing what to type, but the input fields have no placeholders or format examples for email, token, or password.

10.why: Only a single linear method is offered (contact value, token, code, password) with no alternatives such as face login; the individual fields that are presented are clearly labeled.

11.why: Every screen contains exactly one input and one action button, so the user never faces more than one choice at a time.

12.why: Outcomes are communicated via confirmation text ('Your privacy conditions are accepted', 'Appointment request confirmed') and Logs entries, though mid-flow successes are only implied by advancing screens.

13.why: Each step includes a brief guiding sentence plus tips (token expiry, phishing warnings, rate-limit notice), but no dedicated help link or tooltip is provided.

14.why: Step 5 warns verification is 'limited after repeated failures' and no resend-code, back, or retry controls are shown, so easy retry after mistakes is not supported.

15.why: All screens reuse the identical header, card, step indicator, label-input-button structure, Logs panel, and footer without variation.
